subject.title: fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests

question: Should ClickClack JSON REST operations use a fixed 30-second completion deadline while multipart FormData uploads remain unbounded?
rationale: The implementation is sound, but choosing a hard deadline changes behavior for existing slow self-hosted deployments and affects whether late outbound responses are treated as delivery failures.

options.title: Approve the JSON-only deadline
options.body: Accept the private 30-second boundary, preserve the FormData exemption, refresh the branch, and land the proven patch.

options.title: Retune the timeout policy
options.body: Choose a different owner-local duration or define bounded multipart behavior before merging, with updated proof for the selected policy.

options.title: Keep existing unbounded behavior
options.body: Close or pause the PR if ClickClack ownership does not want a fixed REST completion deadline.

recommendation.title: Approve the JSON-only deadline
recommendation.body: Accept the private 30-second boundary, preserve the FormData exemption, refresh the branch, and land the proven patch.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail attributes the original ClickClack runtime implementation to this person, making them the best available owner for the transport-policy choice.
